links.outcome: LLM pneumothorax detection accuracy against thoracic surgeon consensus reference standard
links.effect: ChatGPT sensitivity 100%, specificity 91.4%, PPV 62.5%; Gemini sensitivity 70.0%, specificity 92.9%, PPV 58.3%. Side localisation sensitivity was 14.3% (ChatGPT) and 10.0% (Gemini).
links.quote: The performance of both models in determining the side of pneumothorax was markedly low: ChatGPT had a sensitivity of 14.3%, and Gemini had a sensitivity of 10.0%.

links.outcome: Reliability of multimodal LLM diagnostic output, motivating adjunct rather than stand-alone use
links.effect: Limitations in localisation (sensitivity 10-14%), type determination, and management decisions (tube thoracostomy sensitivity 46.2-57.7%) restrict use to cautious supportive roles.
links.quote: Multimodal LLMs demonstrated high sensitivity in ruling out pneumothorax; however, limitations in agreement, localisation, and management decisions restrict their role to cautious, supportive use under specialist supervision.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic and clinical assessment accuracy of two multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT and Gemini) on retrospective clinical cases with chest X-rays. It does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
